meaning: Starting to learn at sixty is fine. It is never too late.

who: Sawang Janpram, Thai masters athlete · Korea JoongAng Daily, Aug 2026
quote: Sawang Janpram of Thailand began exercising in earnest at 80. At 106 he won world masters gold in discus and javelin: ‘I hope that young people realize the importance of health and exercise every day.’
meaning: He started at 80 and won world gold at 106.

who: Ino Tadataka, mapmaker · Ino Tadataka Museum, Katori City
quote: At 50, Ino Tadataka moved to Edo (old Tokyo) to study astronomy with a teacher 19 years younger. From 55 to 71 his team made 10 surveys of Japan, walking about 40,000 km, roughly once around the Earth.
meaning: He started a new study at 50 and walked across Japan from 55 to 71.

who: Leo Tolstoy · Diary, 1895 and 1897, tr. from Russian
quote: At 66, Leo Tolstoy began learning to ride a bicycle in a Moscow riding hall. It ‘cheers me like a child,’ he wrote, and at 68 he rode to nearby Yasenki: ‘I love this movement very much.’
meaning: Tolstoy learned to ride a bike at 66, and it made him as happy as a child.

quote: Wang Deshun started going to the gym at 50, and at 79 walked his first runway in Beijing. ‘As long as you dare to do things you have never done before, your heart is still young.’
meaning: He started getting fit at 50, and at 79 it opened a new door.

quote: In 1955, at 67, Emma Gatewood became the first woman to hike the whole Appalachian Trail alone. ‘I would never have started this trip if I had known how tough it was, but I couldn't and I wouldn't quit.’
meaning: At 67 she hiked a very long, hard trail. It was tough, but she did not give up.

who: Yuichiro Miura · Guinness World Records; Financial Times, 2017
quote: In his 60s, Yuichiro Miura says, he ate and drank too much and ‘grappled with diabetes’. He trained, and stood on top of Everest at 70, at 75, and in 2013 at 80 years 223 days.
meaning: Unwell in his sixties, he began training and climbed Everest at 80.

who: Mieko Nagaoka · Japan Foundation for Aging and Health, 2015
quote: At 80, fluid in her knee made Noh dance hard, so Mieko Nagaoka took to the pool as rehab: ‘It took me a year to be able to swim 25 metres.’ At 100, she swam 1,500 metres.
meaning: She took up swimming at 80 to help her knee. At 100 she swam 1,500 metres.

quote: After a fall, shingles and heart failure, Kokichi Akuzawa trained with hour-long walks and a mountain almost every week. In August 2025, aged 102, he topped Mount Fuji and later said: ‘It's better to climb while you still can.’
meaning: At 102, after being ill, he trained by walking and climbed Mount Fuji.
